a11y.config_pointer_comment: In most components, the attribute is placed inside `userOptions`
a11y.cursor_pointer_presentation: Applying 'cursor: pointer' to clickable elements such as buttons is a design choice rather than a web standard requirement. Browsers already provide native interaction cues, and altering the cursor changes platform conventions. For this reason, we keep it opt-in, allowing teams to decide based on their design system and user experience goals.

about.p1: Vue Data UI was born of a single question: if your dashboards are so good, why are your users asking for CSV export features ?
about.p2: The purpose of this open-source library is to offer end users a set of in-built tools around charts and tables to reduce the friction of having to recompute exported data. Of course, Vue Data UI keeps the option to export to CSV and PDF, just in case.
about.p3: Vue Data UI offers a set of classic chart types, along with new or rare items, such as
about.p4: To make the experience of your dashboards as smooth as possible, Vue Data UI also ships with a set of utilities, such as
about.alp: Alec Lloyd Probert is a front-end developer, formerly a data analyst, with a strong passion for data visualization and VueJs.

docs.p1: Documentation pages provide you with a config tab where you can tweak your config and save it as JSON. You can also switch from dark to light themes to save configs for both modes.

canvas.description: This chart can be displayed as a SVG or a Canvas.
canvas.detailsDisclaimer: In canvas mode, shapes are not yet available for 'line' and 'plot' types
canvas.details: By default, the configuration will generate a SVG. If you rather have less nodes in your HTML, you can display the chart as a Canvas. This is an experimental feature, you will need to adapt font sizes and chart padding in the options.
canvas.svgAdvantage:
• Vectorized: graphics quality remains the same at all scales.
  • Acessibility: text nodes can be detected by screen readers.
  • Easier debugging, as nodes are part of the DOM
canvas.svgDrawbacks:
• Performance decreases with the number of nodes to paint on the HTML
  • PDF render can be unpredictable for fonts and styling
canvas.canvasAdvantages:
• Stable performance: only one node in the DOM.
  • PDF render is identical.
  • Can be copy pasted as an image
canvas.canvasDrawbacks:
• Image quality does not scale
  • Text elements are not accessible to screen readers
  • Harder debugging as the node is empty in the DOM.

table.fewRows: A few rows as an example

rating.p1: A component to rate, or display rating results. Shows stars by default, and you can use an image if you prefer. You can display as many stars as you want.
rating.p2: In the active mode, the rating can be modified by the user. In readonly mode, it just displays the rating.
rating.simpleRating: If you have a simple rating to display
rating.breakdown: if you have a breakdown per value
rating.calculation: Rating will be calculated based on the breakdown provided.
rating.tooltip: The tooltip can be enabled, to display the values at the hovered item (use in readonly mode).
rating.useImage: or use "image" and provide url in image.src
rating.src: works like the regular src attribute
rating.alt: In image mode, the value of each star will be appended to the provided alt text

skeleton.p1: Placeholders to display while your data is getting fetched
skeleton.smiley: Use smiley icons instead of stars

screenshot.p1: A component to take screenshots in the current page, with 2 modes: download or post.
screenshot.metadata: In post mode, the following metadata will also be provided:
screenshot.quality: don't set it up too high if you care about image size
screenshot.x: the image's top left x coordinate on the page
screenshot.y: the image's top left y coordinate on the page

dashboard.p1: Display your charts in a drag and resize component. Changes can be saved via the @change emit.
dashboard.warning: On embedded VueUiXy and VueUiCandlestick components, it is recommended to disable the zoom functionality in the config, as it conflicts with the dashboard drag events for now.

emits.toggleOpenState: when opening or closing the accordeon, emits the following object to the parent component:
emits.saveAnnotations: emits to the parent component the collection of items currently drawn on the annotator, so they can be saved, and injected back into the component 'dataset' prop later. The emit returns the following attributes:
emits.calledWhen: This emit is called when the user clicks the save button, provided the button is displayed by setting the config.style.showSave to 'true'

annotator.description: Add and save annotations on any slotted content. It works with all 'Vue Data UI' charts, but also with any div, svg, canvas element you place inside.
annotator.warning: Touch events are supported since v.1.7.3, but may be glitchy
annotator.closedState: VueUiAnnotator is in closed state. In the closed state, annotations are invisible, and user interactions with the content is unchanged.
annotator.openState: VueUiAnnotator is in open state. In the open state, all interactions with the slotted content are muted, to allow the user to add, move and resize shapes.
annotator.datastructure: Saved annotations can be passed to the dataset attribute to be displayed onload. Check the 'EMITS' section to learn how to save annotations.
annotator.notByYourself: Important: you should never have to hardcode this dataset, as you can retrieve it from the component's '@saveAnnotations' emit, to save on your database or localStorage.
